messages:
Avery: Quick question - I'm traveling for six weeks and my teletherapist is licensed in CA but not the state I'm temporarily in. I had a video session yesterday and paid out-of-pocket. Will our Redwood plan reimburse OON teletherapy while I'm out of state? Also, can I use EAP for additional sessions while traveling?

Casey (People Ops): Short answer: maybe. Coverage depends on the carrier's licensure/telehealth rules and whether the provider is considered in-network for telehealth in the state where the service occurred. Two paths: 1) If therapist is out-of-network, you can submit for out-of-network reimbursement (we'll need a superbill + proof of payment + provider NPI and taxonomy). 2) If it's a network/licensure issue, sometimes carriers allow temporary telehealth exceptions for travel - we can request an exception.

Avery: What exactly do you need for an OON claim? Is a receipt enough?

Casey (People Ops): For an OON teletherapy reimbursement: (a) Superbills for each session with CPT codes (e.g., 90834, 90837, 90832) and provider NPI; (b) Proof of payment (card statement or receipt); (c) Session date/time and modality (video); (d) A short note if provider couldn't bill carrier due to licensure. Upload all via portal or email benefits@redwood.com with subject "OON teletherapy claim - [Your Name] - [DOS range]". Typical turnaround 7-14 business days after docs received.

Dr. Patel (Therapist): I can provide a CMS-like superbill showing CPT, fee, NPI, and a one-line statement that I cannot bill carrier due to licensure in the client's current state. I recommend adding session notes dates but removing PHI beyond what's needed.

Casey (People Ops): EAP is separate: you can use EAP short-term counseling regardless of travel (EAP vendors typically operate across states). EAP sessions are free and do not require claims submission. If you want an EAP referral, DM me and I'll send contact info.

Avery: And the digital ID card - does it show plan/group for the specialty behavioral network? Provider asked for plan code to check network status.

Casey (People Ops): Yes the PDF/digital ID includes plan name and group number. If your digital card doesn't show the plan code, request a printable ID (we can issue a PDF with the legacy group/plan codes) - email benefits@redwood.com with subject "Printable ID - legacy codes". Also the behavioral network sometimes uses a separate vendor (check the benefits portal under "Behavioral Health Network").

BenefitsBot: Links: upload portal https://benefits.redwood.com/claims/upload (choose "OON mental health"). EAP contact & scheduling: https://benefits.redwood.com/eap. Printable ID: https://benefits.redwood.com/ids/printable.

Avery: Great, I'll ask Dr. Patel for superbills and upload everything. If the carrier denies, can People Ops help with an appeal or exception?

Casey (People Ops): Absolutely - if it's denied we file an appeal or exception request and can escalate to clinical review. If you need immediate support, use EAP in the meantime. Ping me when you upload and I'll track it. :thumbsup:
